topic.title: Bandit Learning with Flexible Feedback
topic.overview: Bandit algorithms learn while acting under limited feedback, balancing immediate performance with information gathering. The represented work varies what can be observed, whether observations cost money, how delays and corruption enter, and whether exploration can be separated from the action whose reward is earned.
topic.whyItMatters: These distinctions change the learning problem substantially. A low-regret policy under full feedback may fail when only a selected action is observed, while extra observation channels can make exploration cheaper than ordinary trial and error.
topic.evolution: The collection includes finite-time and continuum-action analyses, followed by paid advice, cooperation, and dueling feedback. Recent work develops methods that adapt across stochastic and adversarial regimes and handle decoupled exploration. The theoretical gains depend on the stated feedback model rather than transferring automatically between all bandit variants.
openQuestions: How can algorithms adapt when the feedback regime changes during learning?
When is additional observation worth more than another reward-seeking action?

papers.tldr: A clustered bandit policy handles distance-decaying interference with optimal expected regret and a high-probability bound that improves with more units.

papers.title: Near-optimal Regret Using Policy Optimization in Online MDPs with Aggregate Bandit Feedback
papers.tldr: New policy-optimization algorithms achieve optimal known-dynamics regret and substantially improved unknown-dynamics regret using only episode-total losses.

papers.title: Nearly Optimal Algorithms for Contextual Dueling Bandits from Adversarial Feedback
papers.tldr: RCDB learns from adversarially corrupted preference feedback with nearly optimal regret, while a sigmoid-specific refinement improves parameter dependence.

papers.title: No-Regret is not enough! Bandits with General Constraints through Adaptive Regret Minimization
papers.tldr: Weakly adaptive primal and dual learners control general bandit constraints while providing stochastic and adversarial performance guarantees.

papers.title: Policy Optimization for CMDPs with Bandit Feedback: Learning Stochastic and Adversarial Constraints
papers.tldr: A policy-optimization algorithm handles stochastic and adversarial constraints under bandit feedback, with setting-specific theoretical guarantees.

papers.title: Principal-Agent Bandit Games with Self-Interested and Exploratory Learning Agents
papers.tldr: New incentive algorithms provide regret guarantees when self-interested agents learn their rewards and may explore.

papers.title: Tokenized Bandit for LLM Decoding and Alignment
papers.tldr: Tokenized bandit models provide learning guarantees and an almost-optimality result for greedy decoding under the DDMC structural assumption.

papers.title: Tracking Most Significant Shifts in Infinite-Armed Bandits
papers.tldr: Parameter-free bandit guarantees adapt to significant reward shifts, with enhanced rates depending on decreases rather than increases.

papers.title: A Near-optimal, Scalable and Parallelizable Framework for Stochastic Bandits Robust to Adversarial Corruptions and Beyond
papers.tldr: BARBAT improves corruption-robust bandit guarantees while supporting efficient computation and parallelization across several bandit settings.

papers.title: Adapting to Stochastic and Adversarial Losses in Episodic MDPs with Aggregate Bandit Feedback
papers.tldr: New algorithms learn from episode-total losses while achieving optimal stochastic and adversarial regret rates when transitions are known.

papers.title: An Improved Algorithm for Adversarial Linear Contextual Bandits via Reduction
papers.tldr: A reduction yields an efficient contextual bandit algorithm with square-root-in-time regret even when the number of available actions is large.

papers.title: Bandit and Delayed Feedback in Online Structured Prediction
papers.tldr: The paper gives structured-prediction algorithms and regret guarantees for partial or delayed feedback, including a bandit bound independent of output-space size.

papers.title: Constrained Feedback Learning for Non-Stationary Multi-Armed Bandits
papers.tldr: A prior-free bandit algorithm achieves near-optimal dynamic regret when rewards change and feedback queries are budgeted.

papers.title: Data-Dependent Regret Bounds for Constrained MABs
papers.tldr: Data-dependent regret bounds separate the inherent costs of learning and satisfying constraints in bandits with adversarial losses and stochastic constraints.

papers.title: Design-Based Bandits Under Network Interference: Trade-Off Between Regret and Statistical Inference
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes the regret–inference trade-off in networked bandits and proposes an algorithm with an anytime-valid asymptotic confidence sequence.

papers.title: Distributed Multi-Agent Bandits Over Erdős-Rényi Random Networks
papers.tldr: A distributed bandit algorithm achieves logarithmic regret while explicitly accounting for random communication failures and differing rewards across agents.

papers.title: Does Stochastic Gradient really succeed for bandits?
papers.tldr: Stochastic Gradient Bandit's regret depends sharply on its learning rate, with rates above a gap-dependent threshold permitting polynomial regret.

papers.title: Federated Multi-armed Bandits with Efficient Bit-Level Communications
papers.tldr: A two-phase federated bandit algorithm achieves optimal regret guarantees while reducing communication rounds and transmitted bits.

papers.title: Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader Nearly Achieves Best-of-Both-Worlds for the m-Set Semi-Bandit Problems
papers.tldr: Fréchet-perturbed leader selection achieves near-optimal adversarial regret and logarithmic stochastic regret for m-set semi-bandits, with approach-specific lower bounds.

papers.title: From Contextual Combinatorial Semi-Bandits to Bandit List Classification: Improved Sample Complexity with Sparse Rewards
papers.tldr: Sparse rewards enable improved learning guarantees for selecting action subsets with partial feedback, including leading-term full-information rates in a constant-sparsity regime.

papers.title: Greedy Algorithms for Structured Bandits: A Sharp Characterization of Asymptotic Success / Failure
papers.tldr: Partial identifiability exactly characterizes when greedy learning achieves sublinear rather than linear regret in finite structured bandits.

papers.title: Improved Best-of-Both-Worlds Regret for Bandits with Delayed Feedback
papers.tldr: A new delayed-feedback bandit algorithm matches known stochastic and adversarial regret lower bounds up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: Improved Regret and Contextual Linear Extension for Pandora's Box and Prophet Inequality
papers.tldr: New online algorithms improve regret for costly sequential search and extend the guarantees to linear contextual rewards and immediate acceptance decisions.

papers.title: Individual Regret in Cooperative Stochastic Multi-Armed Bandits
papers.tldr: A cooperative bandit algorithm achieves individual regret guarantees independent of communication-graph diameter, including under communication restrictions.

papers.title: Instance-Dependent Regret Bounds for Nonstochastic Linear Partial Monitoring
papers.tldr: The paper derives adversarial partial-monitoring regret bounds that explicitly capture how informative a game’s observations are about its losses.

papers.title: Multimodal Bandits: Regret Lower Bounds and Optimal Algorithms
papers.tldr: A tractable Graves-Lai solver enables asymptotically optimal bandit algorithms when expected rewards have at most m modes.

papers.title: No-Regret Learning Under Adversarial Resource Constraints: A Spending Plan Is All You Need!
papers.tldr: A spending plan enables sublinear regret against plan-following baselines under adversarially changing rewards and resource costs.

papers.title: Non-stationary Bandit Convex Optimization: A Comprehensive Study
papers.tldr: Two algorithms establish strong regret guarantees for changing bandit convex optimization problems, with computational efficiency depending on the loss setting.

papers.title: Non-Stationary Lipschitz Bandits
papers.tldr: A hierarchical bandit algorithm adapts to unknown reward changes and achieves minimax-optimal dynamic regret governed by the number of significant shifts.

papers.title: On the Universal Near Optimality of Hedge in Combinatorial Settings
papers.tldr: Hedge is near-optimal across the stated combinatorial setting, with a precise logarithmic-factor gap that is attained for some action sets.

papers.title: Optimal Regret of Bandits under Differential Privacy
papers.tldr: Private versions of KL-UCB and IMED nearly attain a sharper asymptotic regret lower bound for Bernoulli bandits.

papers.title: Oracle-Efficient Combinatorial Semi-Bandits
papers.tldr: The paper reduces expensive optimization calls in combinatorial semi-bandits to logarithmic or doubly logarithmic growth while preserving strong regret guarantees.

papers.title: Regret Bounds for Adversarial Contextual Bandits with General Function Approximation and Delayed Feedback
papers.tldr: The paper bounds contextual-bandit regret under adversarial feedback delays, including a general regression-oracle result requiring FIFO feedback.

papers.title: Revisiting Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader with Unbounded Perturbations in Bandit Problems
papers.tldr: The paper broadens Best-of-Both-Worlds guarantees for perturbed-leader bandit policies while identifying an obstacle to extending symmetric two-arm results.

papers.title: Taming Adversarial Constraints in CMDPs
papers.tldr: The proposed constrained-learning algorithms achieve guarantees that degrade smoothly with environmental adverseness, even when its level is unknown.

papers.title: Tightening Regret Lower and Upper Bounds in Restless Rising Bandits
papers.tldr: New regret bounds and a rising-concave bandit algorithm narrow the complexity gap while proving this setting harder than stationary bandits.

papers.title: True Impact of Cascade Length in Contextual Cascading Bandits
papers.tldr: The paper proves that contextual cascading-bandit regret decreases for sufficiently long recommendation lists and develops an algorithm with nearly matching theoretical bounds.

papers.title: A Perturbation Approach to Unconstrained Linear Bandits
papers.tldr: A perturbation reduction connects unconstrained linear bandits to online linear optimization and yields new static and dynamic regret guarantees.

papers.title: Bandit Social Learning with Exploration Episodes
papers.tldr: In the studied social-learning model, personally useful exploration within short episodes still fails to produce effective collective learning.

papers.title: Best-of-Both-Worlds for Heavy-Tailed Markov Decision Processes
papers.tldr: Two algorithms provide adaptive regret guarantees for heavy-tailed decision processes with known or, under a stated distributional condition, unknown transitions.

papers.title: Contextual Slate GLM Bandits with Limited Adaptivity
papers.tldr: Efficient contextual slate-bandit algorithms retain strong regret guarantees with very few batches or policy updates.

papers.title: Data-Source Adaptive Online Learning under Heteroscedastic Noise
papers.tldr: SOAR jointly learns good actions and low-noise data sources, approaching best-source bandit regret without knowing that source beforehand.

papers.title: Decentralized Bandits without Global Clock for Dynamic Matching Market
papers.tldr: Way-SE algorithms provide regret guarantees for dynamic matching markets whose participants learn without a global clock.

papers.title: Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader for Decoupled Bandits: Best-of-Both-Worlds and Practicality
papers.tldr: An efficient perturbed-leader policy achieves strong stochastic and adversarial regret guarantees for decoupled bandits without optimization or resampling overhead.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Regret for KL-Regularized Multi-Armed Bandits
papers.tldr: The paper establishes nearly matching regret bounds for KL-regularized bandits and characterizes their transition to square-root scaling under weak regularization.

papers.title: Online Learning with Recency: Algorithms for Sliding-window Streaming Multi-armed Bandits
papers.tldr: Sliding-window bandit theory identifies when limited-memory learning can find approximately best recent options and quantifies memory–regret trade-offs.

papers.title: Online Packet Scheduling with Deadlines and Learning
papers.tldr: Deadline-aware bandit algorithms learn unknown packet values while retaining strong scheduling regret and competitive guarantees.

papers.title: Regret Minimization With a Crowd of Awakening Experts
papers.tldr: Learning with continually arriving experts permits sublinear stochastic regret, but adversarial settings impose a sharper trade-off between regret and competitiveness.

papers.title: Robust Linear Dueling Bandits with Post-serving Context under Unknown Delays and Adversarial Corruptions
papers.tldr: RCDP-UCB combines context prediction and adaptive observation weighting to provide conditional regret guarantees under unknown delays and adversarial corruption.

papers.title: Stochastic Linear Bandits with Parameter Noise
papers.tldr: Parameter-noise linear bandits admit variance-sensitive regret bounds, with a simple explore-exploit algorithm achieving near-optimal rates for specified action balls.

papers.title: Understanding the Gaps in Satisficing Bandits
papers.tldr: Uncertain-UCB sharpens satisficing-bandit regret guarantees when the best option barely exceeds the acceptance threshold.
